items.title: Netanyahu bloc leads as Israeli votes counted, but no majority
items.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival’s opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after two-thirds of the votes were counted in Israel’s pivotal general election . Voters turned out in the highest numbers in decades to give their verdict on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, who has pushed the country sharply to the right and unleashed a wave of wars in response to Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack . Following the vote, both Netanyahu and his main rival Gadi Eisenkot vowed to form a government despite neither being projected to win a majority. With 66 per cent of ballots counted, Netanyahu’s bloc was shown to have 54 of the 120 seats in the parliament. Eisenkot’s opposition bloc had 48 seats and the country’s non-aligned Arab parties 18. The partial results are likely to change as more votes are counted. Exit polls had shown that Eisenkot, a former military chief and political novice, and his opposition bloc were neck-and-neck with Netanyahu’s hard-right camp, with both winning about 51 seats, well away from the threshold for a majority. The strongest gains went to Arab Israeli parties whose voters turned out in soaring numbers against Netanyahu, who has relentlessly warned that the minority would dilute the Jewish nationalist direction in which he has taken Israel. The partial results suggest that Eisenkot’s bloc would have enough seats for a majority if it entered into a coalition agreement with the Arab parties, something most of its members expressed reluctance to do on the campaign trail. But Yair Golan, the head of Israel’s main left-wing party, which is part of Eisenkot’s camp, called for precisely that on Wednesday. “We must no longer accept Netanyahu’s racist division between Jewish votes and Arab votes,” he said on X . “We have a responsibility. And we have an opportunity to form a government of change in partnership with Israel’s Arab citizens.” Eisenkot had said during the campaign he would not govern with Israeli Arab lawmakers, echoing the position of Netanyahu, who has suggested a government relying on Arab votes would lack legitimacy. Arab lawmakers could also give Eisenkot support in parliamentary votes on an ad hoc basis, enabling him to maintain a minority government without joining a coalition. A lack of clear majority for either camp could mean weeks spent trying to cobble together coalitions, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. A stalemate could in the immediate term benefit Netanyahu, who would remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is formed. Full results are expected by Thursday evening or Friday morning. Netanyahu, greeting cheering supporters at a Jerusalem convention centre after 3am (0100 GMT or 6am PKT) on Wednesday morning, called for a “strong government of the right” and said the “Jewish and Zionist majority must unite”. The 77-year-old prime minister, who has governed Israel on and off for nearly two decades, was unusually brief and did not directly claim victory. US President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that his endorsement of Netanyahu had helped “a lot”. A supporter of the Likud party leader and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu waits at the election night rally in Jerusalem on October early on 28, 2026. — AFP ‘Public voted for change’ Speaking to supporters in Tel Aviv, 66-year-old Eisenkot issued a warning to Netanyahu, who observers say could use renewed war to push for a unity government. “Netanyahu, don’t you dare use Israel’s security for your political needs,” Eisenkot said. He called Netanyahu “a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust”. The vote came as Israel faces increasing isolation on the world stage, driven by the wars in Iran and Gaza , as well as soaring settlement construction and violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Eisenkot shares many of Netanyahu’s views on security and has backed the Gaza offensive that has reduced the territory to rubble . But he has vowed to create a more inclusive atmosphere inside Israel, repair its international standing and rein in violent West Bank settlers. After a turnout of nearly 78pc, the highest since 1999, Eisenkot said it would be a mistake to hold a second election and vowed to work “swiftly” to form a government. “The public has voted for change,” he said. “A worthy leader would accept the people’s vote of no confidence and announce his retirement from political life today.” Exit polls had shown Israeli Arab lists projected to win 18 or 19 seats, a sharp gain. Arab Israelis , also known as Palestinian citizens of Israel, account for about 21pc of the country’s population.

items.title: What Is Wrong With Us: A continent cannot be built forever in the future tense
items.description: Africa has never been short of promises, plans or podiums. What its 1.5 billion people need now is proof: lights that stay on, classrooms that teach, and commitments that outlive the ceremonies at which they were announced. By Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng, Chartered Director UK | Chartered Engineer UK | Fellow, Institute of Directors UK | Fellow, Ghana Institution of Engineering | Governance, Industrialisation and Supply Chain Strategist | Founder, Boardroom Governance Summit | Founder and Scriber, NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) A Continent Fluent In The Language Of Tomorrow Africa’s more than 1.5 billion people have heard every promise a podium can produce. They have been promised industrialisation, jobs, affordable housing, reliable electricity, good schools and modern hospitals at election rallies, inaugurations, investment forums and continental summits. Some of those promises were kept, and others produced real if incomplete progress, but far too many remain suspended somewhere between an eloquent speech and a disappointing site visit. Meanwhile, the mother still walks for water, the graduate still searches for work, the entrepreneur still borrows at punishing rates, and the farmer still watches harvests rot for want of storage and roads. And then, another conference is announced, another declaration is drafted, another photograph is taken, and another round of applause fills the hall. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a gentle rebuke: “A promise may inspire hope, but only action improves lives, for no hungry child has ever been fed by a beautifully written development agenda.” The problem is not that Africa plans too much, since planning is essential, but that announcing intentions has quietly become more rewarding, politically and commercially, than delivering outcomes. The Numbers That Should Keep Us Awake At Night The evidence is sobering. The United Nations’ 2024 Africa Sustainable Development Report found that fewer than 6 per cent of the 32 measurable Sustainable Development Goal targets on the continent were on track for 2030, and it warned that gaps in data meant even that verdict was incomplete. According to the most recent global energy tracking reports, roughly 565 million people in sub-Saharan Africa still lacked electricity in 2023, while UNESCO’s 2025 scorecard counted some 118 million African children, adolescents and young people out of school, each of them somebody’s child and somebody’s unrealised future. None of this erases the genuine gains Africa has made in telecommunications, financial inclusion, health and infrastructure, yet progress must never become a comfortable blanket under which complacency sleeps soundly. As NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) warns, “when promises multiply faster than opportunities, citizens stop counting speeches and start counting disappointments.” Ghana And The Tyranny Of The Four-Year Calendar Ghana offers a lesson familiar across the continent. Successive administrations have launched ambitious programmes in industry, infrastructure, education, agriculture and employment, and while some have delivered tangible results, others have stalled amid financing constraints, implementation difficulties or the simple misfortune of having been started by the wrong party. Why should every change of government plunge existing projects into uncertainty? Governments must of course retain the freedom to discard policies that do not work, but they should also possess the maturity to continue worthwhile initiatives regardless of whose name is on the original plaque. A nation’s institutional memory cannot be allowed to expire at every election, because the state belongs to generations rather than to political parties. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) puts it memorably: “a nation cannot build a fifty-year future if, every four years, it behaves as though history has just begun.” Ribbons Are Events, Electricity Is Development Nigeria, blessed with extraordinary human talent, entrepreneurial energy, natural resources and a vast domestic market, shows what Africans achieve when initiative meets opportunity, from its technology founders to its globally celebrated creative industries. Yet tens of millions of Nigerians still lack access to electricity, and many of those who are connected know the familiar roar of the private generator better than the hum of the national grid. Imagine the transformation if reliable power became routine rather than a competitive advantage. South Africa, an advanced industrial economy, learned through years of load shedding how neglected maintenance and weak institutional discipline can dim a nation, and it is now learning that sustained operational focus, new generating capacity and coordinated reform can gradually restore the lights. The lesson for both is identical: political announcements cannot replace engineering, public relations cannot repair a turbine, and no slogan has ever maintained a power station. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes that “cutting the ribbon on a power plant is an event; keeping the lights on is development,” and that “a government may announce transformation in an afternoon, but delivering it takes thousands of disciplined mornings.” Proof That Africa Can Deliver Fairness demands that we celebrate delivery where the evidence supports it. Rwanda’s 2023 to 2024 household survey recorded health insurance coverage of 85.3 per cent, Kenya’s mobile money revolution transformed how ordinary people save, send and borrow, Morocco has built substantial renewable energy and automotive manufacturing capabilities, and Botswana’s diamond governance remains a reference point for how institutions can turn mineral wealth into public value. The real question, then, is not whether Africa can deliver, but why proven approaches are so rarely adapted, financed and sustained elsewhere on the continent. The Promises Made Over Dinner Governments are not the only promise makers who deserve scrutiny. International corporations, investors, consultants and development partners arrive with generous commitments to local employment, technology transfer, skills development, responsible sourcing, environmental protection and supplier participation, and while many honour them admirably, others leave communities wondering whether those undertakings were ever intended to become measurable obligations. Africa must therefore move beyond ceremonial memoranda of understanding and ask harder questions with courteous persistence: how many permanent jobs were created, how many local suppliers became competitive, how many African engineers were trained to advanced levels, how much value was added locally, and how much knowledge remained after the foreign contractor flew home. With trade among African countries still accounting for only around 16 percent of the continent’s exports, according to UN Trade and Development, investment must strengthen Africa’s productive capacity rather than simply expand markets for imported finished goods. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) reminds us that “partnership should mean shared value creation, not merely shared photographs.” We Celebrate The Wrong Scoreboard Perhaps our deepest institutional habit is the celebration of inputs rather than outcomes. We proudly announce how much money was allocated, how many committees were formed, how many agreements were signed and how many delegations travelled, yet citizens are rarely told whether maternal mortality fell, whether children read better, whether journeys became shorter or whether young people found lasting work. A budget is not an achievement merely because it was approved, a policy is not a success merely because it was published, and a summit is not transformative merely because the hotel was fully booked. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) cautions that “a government that confuses expenditure with achievement may discover it has spent a fortune without purchasing progress.” From Ceremonies To A Culture Of Execution The remedy begins with a new discipline of delivery, in which every major public commitment carries defined outcomes, a responsible institution, realistic financing, published milestones and independent review, with progress visible to citizens through accessible public dashboards. Public procurement should reward competence and value for money, contracts should contain enforceable performance obligations, and ministers and chief executives alike should be assessed by measurable results rather than by the frequency of their television appearances. National programmes should be designed to survive political transitions, while continental ambitions such as Agenda 2063 and the African Continental Free Trade Area must be translated into experiences people can feel, from shorter border crossings to seamless payments and harmonised standards, because a trader should never need to read a treaty to discover whether integration is working. The Mirror Every Citizen Must Face Here lies the most uncomfortable question of all, for development cannot be delivered by governments alone. We cannot demand clean cities while emptying refuse into drains, demand accountable institutions while seeking favours that bypass the queue, demand excellent education while shrugging at examination malpractice, or demand industrialisation while dismissing competitive African products in favour of anything bearing a foreign label. This does not absolve leaders of their duties, but it reminds us that progress rests upon a social contract in which leaders deliver, businesses create responsible value, institutions uphold standards and citizens contribute. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) observes, with a knowing smile, that “the citizen who demands national transformation while protecting his own bad habits is asking the country to change on his behalf.” Receipts, Not Reassurances It is time to change what we applaud, honouring functioning hospitals rather than hospital promises, reliable electricity rather than power sector declarations, employable graduates rather than graduation statistics, and enduring institutions rather than personalities whose achievements vanish when they leave office. This is not a demand for miracles, since development requires time, money, competence and hard choices, but it is a demand for honesty, so that a credible leader can say, “this is what we promised, this is what we delivered, this is what remains unfinished, and this is how we will correct it.” One day every president, minister, chief executive and investor will leave office, the banners will come down and the photographs will become archives, and what remains will be the factories that operate, the hospitals that heal, the schools that educate and the institutions that endure for children not yet born. NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom) offers a final reflection: “a promise belongs to the moment it is made, but a fulfilled commitment belongs to generations.” Africa has heard enough about what will be done, and it is time to show what has been done, because a continent’s future cannot be built forever in the future tense. What, then, is wrong with us, and are we finally willing to fix it? ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ing. Professor Douglas Boateng is a pioneering international industrial, manufacturing, and production systems engineer, governance strategist, and Pan-African thought leader whose work continues to influence boardroom thinking, supply chain transformation, and industrialisation strategy across the continent and beyond. As Africa’s first appointed Professor Extraordinaire in Supply Chain Management, he has long championed the integration of procurement, value chain development, industrialisation and governance into national and continental development agendas. An International Chartered Director and Chartered Engineer, he has received numerous lifetime achievement awards and authored several authoritative books. He is the scribe of the globally acclaimed NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom). His work rests on the conviction that Africa’s transformation and the protection of its children will come through deliberate action, strong institutions and leaders willing to build for generations they will never meet. © 2026 Ing. items.title: Transformation économique : les dirigeants de l’Union nationale des Chambres de métiers reçus au palais
items.description: Les dirigeants des quatorze Chambres de métiers du Sénégal, réunies au sein de l'Union nationale des Chambres de métiers, ont été reçus mardi par le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Selon une note de la présidence, les échanges ont porté sur la formation des artisans, la formalisation de leurs activités et l'accès au financement. Le président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a reçu ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, au Palais de la République, les dirigeants des quatorze Chambres de métiers du Sénégal, réunies au sein de l'Union nationale des Chambres de métiers. Établissements publics implantés dans chaque région, les Chambres de métiers encadrent un secteur dont la contribution à l'économie nationale est essentielle. Dans les ateliers de menuiserie, de couture, de mécanique ou de bijouterie, l'artisanat transmet, souligne le texte de la présidence, un savoir-faire de génération en génération et fait vivre des familles dans chaque quartier et chaque village du pays. « Dans chaque atelier, chaque quartier, chaque village du Sénégal, des mains créent, transforment et font vivre notre économie. L’artisanat est une force essentielle de notre souveraineté économique », lit-on dans le texte. A lire aussi : CONFEMEN : une délégation reçue par le président Bassirou Diomaye Faye En réalité, le chef de l'État accorde à ce secteur une place de premier plan dans la transformation économique engagée dans le cadre de la Vision Sénégal 2050. Produire et transformer sur place ce que le pays consomme concourt directement à la souveraineté économique à laquelle il œuvre, et l'artisanat en constitue l'un des ressorts les plus enracinés. Ainsi, les échanges ont porté sur la formation des artisans, la formalisation de leurs activités et l'accès au financement. Dès lors, le président de la République entend accompagner les Chambres de métiers dans cette dynamique, afin que le travail des artisans trouve toute sa place dans la croissance du Sénégal. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Cameroun : sept morts dont quatre civils dans une attaque à Koshin
items.description: © DR Une attaque armée attribuée aux combattants séparatistes a causé la mort de quatre civils le mardi 27 octobre dans cette localité de la région du Nord-Ouest. La riposte de l’armée a permis de neutraliser trois assaillants. L’attaque survenue mardi matin à Koshin, un village situé dans l’arrondissement de Fungom, département de la Menchum, région du Nord-Ouest, a coûté la vie à sept personnes. Des hommes armés ont fait une incursion dans le village, surprenant des habitants dans leur sommeil autour de 2h du matin. Quatre civils ont été tués dans cette attaque à laquelle les forces de défense du Cameroun n’ont pas tardé à riposter. Les éléments du 53è Bataillon d’infanterie motorisée informés de la situation vont tendre une embuscade aux assaillants qui repliaient après avoir commis leur forfait. Les militaires ont ainsi neutralisé trois assaillants. Plusieurs de leurs compagnons ont été blessés avant de prendre la fuite. La réponse de l’armée régulière a permis aussi de saisir d’importantes quantités de matériels militaires : quatre fusils AK-47, deux fusils M21, un fusil de traite, 506 cartouches de calibre AK-47, 165 cartouches de calibre M21, sept chargeurs et des téléphones portables. Cette attaque qui est un signe de la poursuite du conflit ayant déjà duré plus de 10 ans rallonge la liste des victimes civiles estimées à des milliers. La crise dans les régions du Nord-Ouest et du Sud-Ouest résiste encore aux efforts de pacification entrepris depuis 2019. Le Grand dialogue national et ses résolutions, le dialogue communautaire qui vient d’être lancé ainsi que des appels multiples à déposer des armes n’ont pas encore pu mettre fin aux hostilités. Des hommes et des femmes continuent d’être tués, des séparatistes continuent aussi de commettre des actes comme les enlèvements, l’imposition des villes mortes. Cet article Cameroun : sept morts dont quatre civils dans une attaque à Koshin est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Cameroun : Paul Atanga Nji suspend le FSNC à quelques mois des élections législatives et municipales
items.description: © DR Le ministre de l’Administration territoriale, Paul Atanga Nji, a signé un arrêté le 27 octobre portant suspension du Front pour le salut national du Cameroun (FSNC). La décision tombe alors que la scène politique s’active en vue des prochaines élections. Un an après l’élection présidentielle et presque trois mois avant les élections législatives et municipales, le ministre de l’Administration territoriale, Paul Atanga Nji, suspend le Front pour le salut national du Cameroun. L’arrêté ministériel frappe le parti de Issa Tchiroma Bakary pour des actes commis avant, pendant et après l’élection présidentielle du 12 octobre 2026. Le ministre motive sa décision contre le parti politique dont le candidat est classé 2è à la dernière présidentielle par : l’appel à l’insurrection ; atteinte à l’intégrité territoriale, à l’unité nationale et à la souveraineté nationale ; incitation à la violence ayant occasionné des destructions de biens publics et privés ; troubles graves à l’ordre public ; résidence de l’un des dirigeants statutaires à l’étranger. Pour les trois prochains mois, le parti politique est interdit d’exercer toute activité sur le territoire national. Les contrevenants à cette mesure s’exposent à des poursuites judiciaires prévient le ministre en interpellant les autorités administratives de veiller à l’application de cet arrêté. Le gouvernement gèle ainsi les activités du FSNC dont le candidat à la présidentielle et président national a participé à la dernière présidentielle. Démissionnaire du ministère de l’Emploi et de la Formation professionnelle, il a rompu l’alliance avec le régime et s’est lancé à la course pour le fauteuil présidentiel : tentative de nouer des alliances, mobilisation de dernière minute, meetings de campagne fort courus. Au soir du scrutin, le candidat a revendiqué sa victoire avant la proclamation officielle ouvrant un front de contestation. Lequel va se poursuivre avec des manifestations, appels aux villes mortes, dégénérant en crise post-électorale mortelle. Le candidat qui aura pourtant obtenu 35,19% au scrutin et dont l’avenir politique s’annonçait reluisant, va trouver refuge au Nigeria puis en Gambie. A la suite de la présidentielle, il décide, enjoignant son parti à respecter la décision, de boycotter les élections au Cameroun. Notamment les régionales de novembre 2025 et les législatives et municipales qui allaient suivre. Aujourd’hui, le FSNC est suspendu de toute activité au Cameroun. La décision tombe à une période où les acteurs politiques entrent dans l’attente de la convocation du corps électoral pour la tenue des élections législatives et municipales. La mesure survient un an jour pour jour après la proclamation officielle des résultats de la présidentielle de 2025. Elle constitue un obstacle à un déploiement potentiel du parti au cours de cette période qui précède les élections. La non-participation du parti aux prochaines élections entraine des conséquences sur son futur. Il va perdre ses élus locaux et ses députés. Il lui sera difficile de présenter un candidat à la présidentielle de 2032 si les municipales et législatives ne sont pas organisées avant la présidentielle cette année-là. items.title: Mbappe apology taken ‘seriously’ after Mao remark, China says
items.description: China said Wednesday it took “seriously” an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV. Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China and the French player’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing. In a clip of a video interview with French show The Bridge — since taken down — Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao. “My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” the France captain said in a statement in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: “We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made.” La Liga, which saw the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. But that may not be the end of the matter. Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground. CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of the world’s second-richest football league after England’s Premier League. Mbappe’s club also drew fire for not issuing any public apology, with “How much longer will arrogant Real Madrid keep playing ostrich” ranking fifth on search engine Baidu on Wednesday. Real “has neither criticised nor warned Mbappe over his conduct, let alone imposed any disciplinary measures”, the state-run Global Times said in an editorial. Mbappe, 27, continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist. “His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated,” wrote one user on social media platform Weibo. Mbappe’s original joke about Mao was not reposted — or had been scrubbed — from China’s tightly controlled social media. Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe’s account, where he has over a million followers. The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that “the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention”. Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo. An AFP search on Dior and Hublot’s Weibo page with Mbappe’s Chinese name produced no results. – ‘Respect history’ – Offline too the Mbappe brand appeared to be under threat. When AFP visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing’s Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid shirts were available for sale, but none bearing the striker’s name. Chinese state media have previously praised Mbappe as a “footballing sensation” and “talent”. His face is plastered on billboards, on soft drinks and across social media. Mbappe is sometimes affectionately referred to as “Guigui”, meaning “turtle” in Chinese, for his resemblance to a character from the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie. Other major overseas sports leagues have previously angered China. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. “Respecting the history, culture, social customs and national sentiments of others is a fundamental principle for cross-border interaction, a standard of conduct widely upheld by the international community,” the official People’s Daily said in an opinion piece. AFP The post Mbappe apology taken ‘seriously’ after Mao remark, China says appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Ampem Darkoa Ladies arrive in Egypt ahead of final replay against Edo Queens
items.description: Ghana Women’s Premier League champions, Ampem Darkoa Ladies, have arrived in Egypt ahead of the replay of their game against Edo Queens. Ampem Darkoa and Edo Queens will play the 30 minutes of extra time in the WAFU B Women’s Champions League qualifiers after their penalty shootout result was nullified. In a letter addressed to both clubs, CAF referenced the WAFU Zone B qualifying final played on 5 September 2026 and the subsequent decisions of the CAF Organising Committee for Women’s Football dated 26 September 2026 and the CAF Appeal Board dated 16 October 2026. According to CAF, the match will resume from the start of extra time with the score at 2-2, with two periods of 15 minutes to be played, followed by a penalty shoot-out if the score remains level. The Ghanaian side have arrived in Egypt for the encounter to be played in Cairo this week. The winner will stay in Egypt to participate in the main CAF Women’s Champions League tournament.

items.title: Nigerian newspapers review: Tinubu seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
items.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu writing to the Senate to seek approval for a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects nationwide. Another headline reports that the Federal Government and the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) agreed on a series of measures to ease the economic difficulties facing workers, including a ₦70,000 transport intervention and payment of 19 months’ arrears owed to health workers. Vanguard also reports that an independent ministerial committee recommended summary dismissal, administrative sanctions and prosecution of some officers of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) over the deaths of 33 detainees in the custody of its Niger State command in Minna, along with N1.4 billion in compensation for victims and survivors. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian leads with Nigeria’s mounting debt burden coming under heightened scrutiny as President Tinubu seeks legislative approval for fresh external loans of $21.7 billion ($20.52 billion and €1.045 billion), amid rising debt refinancing and little to no savings to liquidate maturing obligations. The Punch reports that Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara asked his supporters to stop referring to him as their leader, declaring that following his reconciliation with his predecessor, Nyesom Wike, he is now a member of the Rainbow Coalition, with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory as its leader. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani declared his readiness to defend Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027, insisting that his support for the president is based on conviction despite public discontent over economic hardship. items.title: Dangote Refinery’s IPO closes with investors from 120 countries
items.description: A Nigerian oil refinery owned by Africa’s richest man Aliko Dangote has closed the continent’s biggest initial public share offering, claiming to have raised funds from investors in 120 countries. The IPO for the Lagos-based Dangote Petroleum Refinery was initially due to close on October 13 but was extended by two weeks to allow more Africans to participate. The company did not disclose how much money was potentially raised by the offering, after saying its target was $1.6 billion. But Aliko Dangote said earlier this month that it had exceeded that goal by “more than three, four times”. “This is a historic achievement for Africa. It shows what is possible when we believe in our continent, work together and invest in our shared future,” he said in a statement late Tuesday. The massive refinery has a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and aims to double its output to 1.4 million barrels per day, potentially making it the world’s largest refinery, surpassing the Jamnagar refinery in India. Investors from all 54 African countries and five other continents participated in the offering, the company said. “Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery,” Aliko Dangote said “The opportunity to own a stake in a major African industrial enterprise has reached investors across every African country and all six inhabited continents,” he added. In July, the refinery secured $2.5 billion in investment from private investors. Last month, the company broke ground on a planned $16 billion refinery on Kenya’s Lamu island, with a projected capacity of 700,000 barrels a day. Africa currently imports more than 70 percent of its refined fuel, according to an Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) report in April. items.title: Nationalité française : le nouveau décret de naturalisation est tombé, ce qui change
items.description: En France, un nouveau décret de naturalisation , de réintégration et de francisation vient d'être officialisé, s'accompagnant d'un encadrement strict de la publication des noms pour protéger la vie privée des nouveaux citoyens. Il a été publié au Journal officiel. Un sésame tant attendu Pour des milliers de demandeurs, c'est l'aboutissement d'un parcours du combattant de plusieurs mois, voire de plusieurs années. Le décret officiel portant attribution de la nationalité française , réintégrations et extensions aux enfants mineurs a été publié. Derrière ce texte administratif se cachent des destins bouleversés et l'officialisation d'un nouveau chapitre de vie pour de nouveaux Français. L’accès protégé : la fin du grand déballage public La grande spécificité de ce type de décret réside dans ses modalités de consultation. Contrairement aux lois ou décrets réglementaires classiques, les listes nominatives des nouveaux naturalisés ne sont plus librement et massivement aspirées par les moteurs de recherche. En application des règles de protection des données personnelles et des dispositions du code des relations entre le public et l'administration, l'accès à ce Journal officiel se fait désormais sous un régime protégé : Consultation restreinte : Les listes sont accessibles directement sur le portail officiel Légifrance, mais nécessitent des vérifications pour éviter l'indexation massive des nom-prénoms par Google ou consorts. Démarche individuelle : Chaque impétrant doit consulter personnellement son statut. Aucune association, aucun intermédiaire ne peut effectuer cette vérification à la place des usagers. Comment savoir si votre nom y figure ? Si vous ou un proche attendez l'officialisation de votre naturalisation : Rendez-vous directement sur la page officielle du décret sur Légifrance . Connectez-vous à votre compte si nécessaire pour accéder aux documents en mode sécurisé. Gardez à l'esprit que les parutions se font par vagues : l'absence de votre nom sur ce décret précis ne signifie en aucun cas un refus définitif, mais simplement que votre dossier suit son cours dans une autre promotion. L’article Nationalité française : le nouveau décret de naturalisation est tombé, ce qui change est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Dékheulé : ici, tombait Lat Dior il y a 140 ans
items.description: Situé à cheval entre les communes de Darou Marnane et de Thilmakha, à quatre kilomètres de la route nationale, Dekheulé est une terre chargée d’histoire. C’est ici que Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop, Damel du Cayor, a livré sa dernière bataille contre les troupes coloniales françaises avant de tomber les armes à la main, le 27 octobre 1886, en défendant son peuple contre la domination coloniale. Un monument funéraire abritant son mausolée et un musée historique y ont été érigés pour perpétuer sa mémoire et célébrer le courage de ce héros national. Cent-quarante ans après sa disparition, le Sénégal s’apprête à rendre hommage à l’un des symboles de la résistance à la colonisation. Reportage. Ce 24 octobre 2026, le ciel s’est paré d’un bleu clair. La chaleur se fait sentir dès les premières heures de la matinée, en cette période qui marque la fin de l’hivernage. Les rayons ardents du soleil accentuent davantage cette sensation. Nous sommes à Dekheulé, une localité située à cheval entre les communes de Darou Marnane et de Thilmakha. L’évocation de ce nom renvoie immédiatement à Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop, le Damel du Cayor. C’est sur cette terre qu’il a livré sa dernière bataille contre les troupes coloniales françaises, le 27 octobre 1886, avant de mourir les armes à la main. Pour s’y rendre, il faut, une fois à Darou Mouhty, dans le département de Kébémer, parcourir une vingtaine de kilomètres jusqu’à la sortie de Darou Marnane, puis bifurquer à gauche pour emprunter une piste latéritique en très mauvais état sur quatre kilomètres. Tout au long du trajet, le visiteur admire la splendeur de la nature, marquée par un immense tapis herbacé qui s’étend à perte de vue. Toutefois, la verdure jaunit progressivement sous l’effet de la chaleur. Par endroits, des champs de mil et d’arachide se dessinent dans le paysage. Leurs propriétaires ont commencé les récoltes. Les épis de mil ont été coupés, tandis que les fanes d’arachide sont regroupées çà et là dans les champs. Le temps semble suspendu. Le murmure des arbres se fait à peine entendre, tant le vent est absent. Aucune feuille ne voltige. Après quelques minutes à bord d’un taxi-brousse, Dekheulé se dévoile enfin. Le village présente un mélange d’habitations traditionnelles en cases et de maisons en dur. Ici, les populations mènent une vie austère et vivent principalement de l’agriculture et de l’élevage. Mais, au-delà de cette apparente tranquillité, la localité occupe une place importante dans l’histoire du Sénégal. C’est ici que se trouve le mausolée de Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop, l’une des figures emblématiques de la résistance à la colonisation française. Un lieu chargé d’histoire Sur place, le visiteur remarque d’abord un mur de clôture entourant le site. On y découvre la devise du Sénégal, inscrite en lettres capitales, ainsi que les noms ou les représentations de figures historiques de la résistance, parmi lesquelles Cheikh Ahmadou Bamba et Maba Diakhou Bâ. Accueillis par Thierno Diop, un des descendants de Lat Dior, nous entamons la visite de ce lieu classé au patrimoine historique national. Notre guide nous conduit d’abord devant le monument funéraire. «C’est ici que repose notre aïeul, Lat Dior », explique-t-il en désignant le mausolée, matérialisé par une stèle aux teintes rougeâtres. Cette couleur évoquerait le sang du Damel versé sur ce champ de bataille. Quelques inscriptions sont gravées dans le marbre. Le monument funéraire a été construit sous la présidence d’Abdou Diouf, qui l’a inauguré le 27 octobre 1986, en présence du ministre de la Culture de l’époque, Makhily Gassama. La cérémonie coïncidait avec le centenaire de la disparition de Lat Dior. La visite se poursuit au musée, situé à proximité du mausolée. « C’est un bâtiment composé de deux pièces », précise Thierno Diop, qui exprime sa reconnaissance à l’État du Sénégal pour avoir érigé ce musée en hommage à son aïeul. Construit par le ministère de la Culture et inauguré le 22 décembre 2018 par le président Macky Sall, le musée historique de Dekheulé constitue un lieu de mémoire consacré à la résistance du Damel du Cayor face à l’oppression coloniale. A lire aussi : Commune de Guet Ardo : faute d’enseignants, l’école du village Thialaga Niane fermée Lat Dior occupe une place importante dans l’histoire nationale en raison de son engagement contre l’expansion coloniale française. De son accession au trône, en juillet 1862, à son ultime combat à Dekheulé, le 27 octobre 1886, il a défendu la souveraineté du Cayor, notamment en s’opposant au projet de construction du chemin de fer Dakar-Saint-Louis. Le Damel est ainsi resté célèbre pour son courage, sa détermination et sa résistance à la domination française. Pour Thierno Diop, son combat symbolise le refus de la soumission, la dignité, la liberté et la défense de la souveraineté du peuple sénégalais. Ce héros de la résistance, estime-t-il, mérite d’être davantage célébré et enseigné dans les écoles afin de servir d’exemple aux générations futures. Un site confronté à des difficultés d’accès Malgré l’érection du monument funéraire et la construction du musée historique, force est de constater que le site de Dekheulé a encore besoin d’un accompagnement pour assurer sa promotion et sa valorisation. Pour Thierno Diop, petit-fils de Lat Dior, cette situation s’explique notamment par l’enclavement de la localité. Situé à environ quatre kilomètres de la route nationale, le site est difficile d’accès en raison du mauvais état de la piste latéritique. Cette contrainte décourage de nombreux visiteurs. « Nous voulons que la route soit praticable afin de faciliter l’accès au site », plaide-t-il, appelant les autorités à répondre à cette doléance. Selon lui, l’aménagement de cette piste permettrait d’attirer davantage de visiteurs et de faire connaître ce haut lieu de mémoire. Dans la même dynamique, Saer Diop, lui aussi descendant de Lat Dior, estime que Dekheulé pourrait devenir un véritable site touristique, capable d’accueillir quotidiennement des visiteurs venus d’horizons divers. C’est dans cette perspective que l’Association générale pour la sauvegarde des valeurs de Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop, héros national du Sénégal (Agehn), a retenu cette année le thème suivant : « Dekheulé, 140 ans après : du mémoriel au musée, valorisation du patrimoine et du tourisme culturel ». Cette thématique vise à ouvrir la réflexion sur les stratégies à mettre en œuvre pour promouvoir et valoriser ce site historique. Ce que ses descendants sollicitent de l’État Chaque année, l’Association générale pour la sauvegarde des valeurs de Lat Dior Ngoné Latyr Diop (Agehn) organise la commémoration de la disparition du Damel du Cayor. L’édition de 2026 revêt un caractère particulier puisqu’elle marque le 140ᵉ anniversaire de sa mort. À travers le thème « Dekheulé, 140 ans après : du mémoriel au musée, valorisation du patrimoine et du tourisme culturel », l’association entend contribuer à la préservation et à la transmission de la mémoire de Lat Dior, tout en favorisant la promotion du patrimoine historique et culturel lié à Dekheulé. Pour assurer le bon déroulement de cet événement annuel et donner davantage de visibilité à ce haut lieu de mémoire, les descendants de Lat Dior sollicitent le soutien et l’accompagnement de l’État. Ils espèrent ainsi que les autorités contribueront à améliorer l’accessibilité du site et à renforcer sa valorisation touristique et culturelle. Au-delà de la commémoration, l’enjeu est de faire de Dekheulé un espace vivant de transmission de l’histoire nationale, où les générations présentes et futures pourront découvrir l’héritage d’un homme qui a marqué la résistance sénégalaise à la colonisation. Par Falel PAM

items.title: BRICS won’t be a magic wand for Ghana; corruption and irregularities in public finances pose a threat
items.description: The government of Ghana under President John Dramani Mahama has applied to join BRICS as a partner. The country’s Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa argues that the decision forms part of the government’s efforts to expand Ghana’s economic options and diversify its international partnerships. “The major highlight, which I am disclosing to the Ghanaian people for the first time, is that the Cabinet of President John Dramani Mahama has decided that Ghana will be joining BRICS,” he said. Ablakwa and many government officials express the view that Ghana’s membership of the bloc, which brings together major emerging economies, could provide the country with alternative economic and diplomatic partnerships. We believe that joining India in BRICS will give us economic options, will diversify our base and our partnerships, and will also allow us to have more cooperation within the Global South framework, as far as South-South engagements are concerned. This announcement by the Foreign Affairs Minister’s signalled Ghana’s intention to deepen its engagement with emerging economies as the government seeks to broaden the country’s international economic partnerships. BRICS comprises Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa and seeks to strengthen economic, political and diplomatic cooperation among its members. Therefore, partnering with BRICS may open new economic avenues for Ghana, including trade diversification, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI), and alternative development financing. Ghana already enjoys excellent relations with the BRICS member countries. Therefore, it will be joining natural allies in a bloc that arguably is the largest trading bloc today. But there are some concerns that need to be addressed. Ghana risks becoming a market for powerful BRICS economies and exposing its natural resources to further exploitation without a clear industrial strategy. While joining BRICS could expand Ghana’s trade and investment opportunities, the natural resource-rich West African country may end up benefiting less than industrial giants such as China, India, Brazil and Russia. BRICS brings together eleven major emerging markets and developing countries of the world: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and United Arab Emirates. It will therefore serve as a useful platform for consultation and cooperation on contemporary issues having global, as well as regional significance, and issues of global political and economic governance. Concerns were also raised that this decision will affect Ghana’s relations with its traditional partner countries who have ideological differences with the BRICS member countries. However, Ghanaian authorities explain that the decision affirms Ghana’s policy of non-alignment, which enabled President Kwame Nkrumah, at the height of the Cold War, to navigate the terrain to secure the support of the United States to build the Akosombo Dam, while at the same time getting the then Soviet Union (Russia) to launch Africa’s pioneering atomic energy programme, the Ghana Nuclear Reactor Project (GNRP). Despite the optimism, the point ought to be made that joining BRICS will not be a magic wand for Ghana’s economic problems. Corruption There are several factors that will not include corruption. Corruption poses a grave threat to the stability, development, and integrity of Ghanaian society. It deprives the country of the needed development. To that end, if Ghana is to really benefit from joining BRICS, effort will have to be made to fight corruption. If expatriate investors come into the country as a result of BRICS membership, yet they are subjected to corruption practices in business registration and work permits, these businesses will eventually get frustrated and exit the country. Recently, the National Commission for Civic Education (NCCE) indicated that Ghana loses more than US$3 billion every year through corruption. According to the NCCE, the resources lost through corruption could instead be invested in infrastructure, job creation and essential services, where the demand for development remains high. This comment highlights the point that in order for BRICS membership to fully benefit Ghana, corruption will have to be addressed. It is for this reason also that the Office of the Special Prosecutor advocates the efficacy of investigations and prosecutions in curbing corruption. The OSP also recognises that transforming Ghana’s culture of corruption requires a comprehensive, large-scale prevention programme. The Office, as mandated by Section 2(c) of the Office of the Special Prosecutor Act, 2017 (Act 959), is dedicated to taking proactive measures to prevent corruption. Poor management of public finances The other threats to the benefits of BRICS are issues with irregularities in the public financial system in Ghana, as captured in the Auditor-General’s reports. Recently, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) highlighted GH₡5.2 billion in irregularities, with GH₡4.8 billion on tax infractions recorded in the 2025 audit report. The committee’s chair, Abena Osei-Asare, expressed concern about the recurrence of similar audit findings involving public institutions, and said such development gave a clear indication that MDAs were not learning their lessons. “If the same institution is cited repeatedly for the same control failure, then we are no longer dealing with just audit findings; we are dealing with a failure to learn,” she pointed out. The irregularities in the public finances have been prevalent and appear in the auditors’ general reports year in and year out. The issues seem unresolved because surcharges are unpaid. Abena Osei-Asare says a total of GH¢280.5 million in surcharges following audit reports remains unpaid. Information from the Audit Service showed that GH¢280.5 million in surcharges remained uncollected. About GH¢57.2 million had been collected through the Auditor-General’s recovery accounts since 2022, as of February 2026. Definitely, if issues in public finance management aren’t resolved, the benefits of BRICS will be an illusion to the government and the people of Ghana. Because the revenues that will accrue from the FDIs may not be properly accounted for by the state agencies. Stronger internal controls across public institutions to prevent financial irregularities and safeguard public funds will be key in ensuring the benefits of BRICS partnership are realised. Effective internal auditing was critical to ensuring that public resources were properly managed and channelled into development priorities under the government’s New Economy agenda. Geopolitical concerns Concerns are that Ghana’s attempt to join BRICS will affect Ghana’s relations with its traditional partner countries who have ideological differences with the BRICS member countries. The question is, is BRICS’s partnering status a means for a safe pragmatic stepping stone for a balanced foreign policy, diversifying the economy or just for a half-measure that lacks real decision-making power? Hence, will this move by Ghana damage its established sources of loans, grants/Aids from the Western Bloc/ International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank and access to Western Markets of the USA (especially AGOA) and the markets of the European Union for her products, which are needed by the thousands of Ghanaians, other Africans, and offspring of Africans in the Western Countries and Countries of their allies? There are also the Constitutional and Historical Questions, which Ghana needs to take note of in its attempt to join BRICS. Ghana needs to take note of Article 40 of the 1992 Constitution, which guides Ghana’s foreign policy to promote and protect national interests and Ghana’s historical non-alignment policy, which saw President Kwame Nkrumah’s historical playbook of non-alignment by balancing ties with the Western Bloc and the Eastern Bloc, which saw Ghana obtaining financial and technical support from the West, especially the USA, for projects like the Akosombo Dam and its early nuclear cooperation with the East. So, the real litmus test is: when Ghana is granted the Partner Status, can Ghana use the platform of the BRICS to transform its raw exports into localised industrial capacity without burning bridges with traditional Western financiers. About BRICS BRICS is an international organisation currently comprising ten countries: Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Its conceptual origins were articulated by Russian foreign minister Yevgeny Primakov in 1998, and can be traced to informal forums and dialogue groups such as RIC (Russia, India, and China) and IBSA (India, Brazil, and South Africa). BRIC was originally a term coined by British economist Jim O’Neill, and later championed by his employer Goldman Sachs in 2001, to designate a group of emerging markets. The bloc’s inaugural summit was held in 2009 and featured the founding countries of Brazil, Russia, India, and China; they adopted the acronym BRIC and formed an informal diplomatic group where their governments could meet annually at formal summits and coordinate multilateral policies. South Africa joined the organisation in September 2010, which was then renamed BRICS, and attended the third summit in 2011 as a full member. Iran, Egypt, Ethiopia, and the United Arab Emirates attended their first summit as member states in 2024 in Russia. Indonesia officially joined in early 2025, becoming the first Southeast Asian member. Saudi Arabia was invited to the Johannesburg summit, and it is considered part of the organisation, but has not publicly confirmed its membership. The term BRICS+ has been informally used to reflect new membership since 2024. Collectively, BRICS comprises more than a quarter of the global economy and nearly half the world’s population.

items.title: Four die; seven injured in Lagos accidents
items.description: Four persons died and seven others sustained injuries in three separate road accidents in Lagos on Wednesday, the Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) has said. The ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌⁠​​‍​​‌​agency said the fatal accident occurred at Berger Bridge, inward Eleko, along the Ibeju-Lekki Expressway, involving an articulated truck conveying a 20-foot container and an interstate Toyota Hiace bus. LASEMA’s Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Oke-Osanyintolu, confirmed the incidents in a statement made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Wednesday in Lagos. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency received a distress call and immediately activated its response team from Epe Base to the scene. According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that the truck was ascending the bridge at excessive speed when it collided with the bus. He said the truck driver lost control while attempting to avoid the collision, causing the truck to overturn onto the bus. Oke-Osanyintolu said four adult males died at the scene, while six other adult males sustained varying degrees of injuries. He said LASEMA, alongside the Federal Road Safety Corps and the Nigeria Police Force, secured the scene and administered first aid to the injured. He said the injured persons were subsequently conveyed to Epe General Hospital for further medical attention, he said. Oke-Osanyintolu added that a private crane had been secured to recover the overturned truck and container and facilitate the safe extrication of the deceased. He said the recovery operation was ongoing, with traffic management measures deployed to ensure safety along the corridor. In a related development, he said LASEMA’s Tiger Team from C3 Base responded to a truck accident at about 4:09 a.m. near Vetland School, inward Agege Pen Cinema, along Old Abeokuta Road. He said the truck, with registration number KTU-940XT, rammed into a solar-powered streetlight pole before mounting the road median and obstructing traffic. He said that preliminary findings attributed the incident to reckless driving, although no casualty was recorded. Oke-Osanyintolu said the agency deployed traffic diversion measures and later recovered the truck using its heavy-duty equipment, Elephant. He said the truck was conveyed to Abattoir Police Station for further investigation and safekeeping. The permanent secretary also said LASEMA’s Beta Team from Igando Base responded to another accident at Lanre Bus Stop, inward Igando, along LASU-Igando Road. He said the accident involved a DAF truck, with registration number SMK 795 XY, and a Toyota Corolla, with registration number AKD 169 EA. According to him, a broken-down truck on the opposite side of the road had caused traffic congestion when the DAF truck, allegedly driving against traffic, collided with the Corolla. He said the collision obstructed half of the road inward in Igando, while the Corolla driver sustained a minor head injury. “The injured driver was taken to Igando General Hospital by an associate,” Oke-Osanyintolu said. He added that the Corolla had been towed to Igando Police Station, while LASEMA deployed its heavy-duty equipment, Super Metro, to recover the DAF truck and restore traffic flow. Oke-Osanyintolu said the recovery operation was ongoing. He urged motorists to observe speed limits, avoid driving against traffic and reckless manoeuvres, and ensure their vehicles were mechanically sound before embarking on any journey. He also advised residents to report emergencies through the state’s toll-free lines, 767 and 112. The permanent secretary commiserated with the families of the deceased and wished the injured persons a speedy recovery. (NAN) The post Four die; seven injured in Lagos accidents appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Conakry : la Türkiye célèbre les 103 ans de sa République et réaffirme son ambition de renforcer sa coopération avec la Guinée
items.description: L’ambassade de la République de Türkiye en Guinée a célébré, mardi 27 octobre 2026, le 103ᵉ anniversaire de la proclamation de la République turque. La cérémonie, organisée dans un réceptif hôtelier de Conakry, a réuni des membres du corps diplomatique, des représentants des autorités guinéennes, des responsables des forces de défense et de sécurité ainsi que plusieurs personnalités des deux pays. Au-delà de la commémoration historique, cette rencontre a permis de réaffirmer les liens d’amitié et de coopération entre Conakry et Ankara, notamment dans les domaines économique, éducatif, technologique et environnemental. La cérémonie a débuté par la projection d’une vidéo promotionnelle consacrée à la Türkiye, avant l’allocution officielle de Son Excellence Cem Ornekol, ambassadeur de la République de Türkiye près la République de Guinée. Dans son intervention, le diplomate turc est revenu sur la portée historique du 29 octobre 1923, date de proclamation de la République sous la conduite de Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Il a rappelé les valeurs fondatrices de son pays, notamment la souveraineté, la démocratie, la solidarité et la paix. « Le 29 octobre 1923 marque un moment fondateur de l’histoire de la nation turque. Sous la direction de Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, notre peuple a choisi de bâtir un État souverain, moderne et tourné vers l’avenir. La République est née d’une volonté collective : celle de faire confiance au savoir, au travail, à la citoyenneté et à la capacité de chaque génération de contribuer au progrès de son pays », a-t-il déclaré. Abordant les relations bilatérales, l’ambassadeur a salué la qualité du partenariat entre la Türkiye et la Guinée, qu’il souhaite voir se consolider davantage à travers des projets concrets et mutuellement bénéfiques. « Cette célébration est aussi l’occasion de saluer les liens d’amitié qui unissent la Türkiye et la Guinée. Nos deux pays entretiennent une relation fondée sur le respect mutuel, la solidarité et la volonté de construire des partenariats utiles à nos peuples. Dans les domaines politique, économique, sécuritaire, éducatif, culturel et du développement, nous poursuivons nos échanges avec confiance et dans un esprit de coopération bénéfique mutuelle », a-t-il souligné. Pour le diplomate, la valorisation des ressources naturelles guinéennes doit nécessairement s’accompagner d’investissements dans le capital humain. Il a particulièrement insisté sur la formation des jeunes, le développement des compétences scientifiques et numériques ainsi que l’adaptation aux mutations technologiques. « La Guinée possède une jeunesse dynamique et riche de talents. Elle constitue l’une des forces majeures du pays et un atout essentiel pour son avenir. La Guinée dispose également de ressources naturelles exceptionnelles. Mais, aussi précieuses soient-elles, ces ressources ne deviennent durables que lorsqu’elles s’accompagnent d’investissements dans l’éducation des jeunes générations, dans les compétences des femmes et des hommes, les institutions et la connaissance », a expliqué Cem Ornekol. Dans cette perspective, l’ambassadeur a mis en avant les opportunités offertes aux étudiants guinéens par le programme de bourses Türkiye, qui leur permet de poursuivre des études supérieures dans les universités turques. Il a également salué la contribution de l’École Maarif de Conakry au secteur éducatif. Sur le plan économique, Cem Ornekol a fait état d’une progression significative des échanges commerciaux entre les deux pays au cours des trois dernières années. « Sans vouloir vous inonder de statistiques, je me permettrai de préciser que le volume de nos échanges commerciaux bilatéraux a progressé de plus de 35 % ces trois dernières années. Au vu de cette dynamique, nous anticipons qu’il dépassera les 350 millions de dollars à la fin de 2026. Il y a dix ans, lors de sa visite en Guinée, le président Erdoğan avait exprimé l’ambition de porter nos échanges à 500 millions de dollars […] convaincu que cet objectif pourrait être atteint prochainement grâce à l’implication des entreprises turques déjà installées en Guinée, à l’arrivée de nouveaux investisseurs et au renforcement des partenariats avec les opérateurs économiques guinéens », a-t-il indiqué. Il a également évoqué les interventions de l’Agence turque de coopération et de coordination (TİKA) dans les secteurs de la santé, de l’éducation, de l’agriculture et du renforcement des capacités. À cela s’ajoute la contribution de Turkish Airlines, qui assure, selon lui, quatre liaisons hebdomadaires entre Conakry et Istanbul, facilitant ainsi les déplacements et les échanges entre les deux peuples. Sur les questions environnementales, Cem Ornekol a évoqué l’accueil par la Türkiye de la 31ᵉ Conférence des Parties sur les changements climatiques (COP31), prévue à Antalya du 9 au 20 novembre 2026, tout en exprimant le souhait d’y voir participer une délégation guinéenne. Concluant son intervention sur un message de paix et de fraternité, l’ambassadeur a rappelé cette devise de Mustafa Kemal Atatürk : « Paix dans le pays, paix dans le monde. » La Guinée réaffirme son engagement en faveur d’un partenariat renforcé Prenant la parole au nom du ministre des Affaires étrangères, de l’Intégration africaine et des Guinéens établis à l’étranger, Dr Morissanda Kouyaté, Mariama Bailo Barry a transmis les félicitations du gouvernement et du peuple guinéens à la Türkiye à l’occasion de cette célébration. Elle a salué le parcours historique du peuple turc ainsi que les relations de confiance, de respect mutuel et de solidarité qui unissent les deux nations. « Les relations entre la République de Guinée et la République de Turquie reposent sur une solide tradition d’amitié, de respect mutuel et de solidarité. Elles traduisent notre volonté commune de bâtir un partenariat constructif fondé sur la confiance, le dialogue et des intérêts mutuellement bénéfiques », a-t-elle déclaré. Au nom des autorités guinéennes, la diplomate a réaffirmé l’engagement du gouvernement à poursuivre et à approfondir cette coopération, conformément aux ambitions de développement national. « Je saisis cette heureuse occasion pour réaffirmer la disponibilité du gouvernement guinéen, sous le leadership de Son Excellence le président général Mamadi Doumbouya, président de la République, chef de l’État, à poursuivre avec la partie turque un dialogue régulier et constructif, afin de donner à notre partenariat une portée toujours plus concrète et des résultats plus visibles pour nos populations », a-t-elle affirmé. Évoquant les priorités nationales, Mariama Bailo Barry a souligné la convergence entre les ambitions de développement des deux pays. Elle a notamment insisté sur la nécessité d’orienter davantage la coopération économique vers la création de richesses et d’emplois, en cohérence avec les objectifs du programme Simandou 2040. « Nous souhaitons que notre coopération s’oriente davantage vers des investissements productifs, la transformation locale de nos ressources et le transfert collectif des compétences et de technologies afin de créer davantage de valeur ajoutée en République de Guinée », a-t-elle soutenu. Elle a salué la présence des entreprises turques dans plusieurs secteurs de l’économie guinéenne, tout en encourageant de nouveaux partenariats entre investisseurs turcs et opérateurs économiques nationaux. L’objectif de porter les échanges commerciaux bilatéraux à 500 millions de dollars, précédemment exprimé par le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, a également été présenté comme une perspective encourageante. Reconnaissant les efforts consentis par la Türkiye dans le domaine éducatif, la diplomate guinéenne a plaidé pour un élargissement des opportunités offertes aux jeunes. « Le capital humain demeure le fondement le plus durable de la prospérité d’une nation. À cet égard, nous apprécions les opportunités de formation offertes aux étudiants guinéens à travers le programme de bourses turques, et souhaitons que cette coopération s’élargisse aux domaines scientifique, de l’ingénierie, de la santé, de la formation technique et du numérique », a-t-elle précisé. Elle a également salué les actions de TİKA et la contribution de l’École Maarif de Conakry à l’enseignement et au rapprochement entre les deux sociétés. Concernant les enjeux environnementaux, Mariama Bailo Barry a exprimé le soutien de la Guinée à l’organisation de la COP31 en Türkiye, en mettant particulièrement l’accent sur les attentes des pays en développement. « Nous formulons le vœu que cette rencontre favorise des solutions concrètes et une mobilisation accrue des financements nécessaires à l’adaptation climatique, en particulier aux profils des pays en voie de développement », a-t-elle indiqué. Pour terminer, la représentante du chef de la diplomatie guinéenne a renouvelé les félicitations des autorités nationales au gouvernement et au peuple turcs, tout en exprimant le souhait de voir cette coopération produire davantage de résultats au profit des populations. « Je formule le vœu que les relations entre nos deux pays continuent de se renforcer et que notre coopération produise des résultats toujours plus tangibles au bénéfice de nos populations, en particulier de notre jeunesse, à qui nous devons léguer un avenir porteur d’opportunités, de dignité et d’espérance », a-t-elle conclu. À la suite de cette intervention, l’ambassade de Türkiye a organisé un tirage au sort à l’issue duquel un citoyen guinéen a remporté un voyage lui permettant de découvrir le pays. Cette célébration du 103ᵉ anniversaire de la République de Türkiye aura ainsi constitué un moment de convivialité diplomatique, mais également une occasion pour les deux pays de réaffirmer leur volonté commune de consolider un partenariat fondé sur le dialogue, les investissements, le transfert de compétences et le développement durable. Mayi Cissé L’article Conakry : la Türkiye célèbre les 103 ans de sa République et réaffirme son ambition de renforcer sa coopération avec la Guinée est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Aucun nouveau cas positif d’Ebola enregistré depuis huit jours à Mongwalu en Ituri
items.description: Aucun nouveau cas positif de la maladie à virus Ebola n’a été enregistré depuis le 18 octobre au centre de traitement de Mongwalu, en Ituri, selon des sources médicales. items.title: Haris Rauf penalised for breach of ICC Code of Conduct in tri-series match against England
items.description: Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf has been fined 20pc of his match-fee for breaching the International Cricket Council (ICC) Code of Conduct during the One-day International (ODI) tri-series match against England on Sunday. According to an ICC media released issued on Wednesday, Haris was found to be in breach of Level 1 of the code for appealing for a wide from the n0n-striker’s end in the 46th over and argued with England all-rounder Will Jacks after it was denied. The ICC said Haris ignored the warning given from on-field umpire Sharfuddoula and continued arguing, and also raised his bat in frustration. The right-armer, whose stand of seven off 19 balls played a crucial role in Pakistan’s one-wicket victory in the match along with Shadab Khan’s century effort, also received a demerit point as part of his penalty, which he incurred after breaching Article 2.20 of the Code of Conduct, that pertains to “displaying conduct that is contrary to the spirit of the game”. This was his third offence in a 24-month period, taking his overall tally of demerit points to five. Haris accepted his offence, as well as the sanctions proposed by Jeff Crowe of the Emirates ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees, and hence there was no formal hearing, the ICC release read. England, meanwhile, were penalised 15pc of their match-fee for a slow over rate, after being found three overs short at the allocated time. Captain Harry Brook accepted the offence and the sanction as well, the ICC said.

items.title: Karim Zito sacked over inconsistent results and disunity among backroom staff – AshantiGold CEO
items.description: AshantiGold Chief Executive Officer Edward Kwasi Akuoko has attributed the dismissal of Karim Zito and his assistants to inconsistent results and disunity among the backroom staff. The Obuasi-based club announced the decision in a statement on October 27, relieving the former Asante Kotoko coach and his two assistants, Ernest Okyere and Robert Dabuo, of their duties following a consultative meeting of the Interim Management Committee. AshantiGold have made a mixed start to the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League campaign, recording three wins in their opening eight matches. They currently sit 11th on the league table with 11 points. “As a serious club, you always want to win,” Akuoko told Obaapa Radio. “I’m not a leader who always lowers expectations just because we are a newly promoted side. We are not saying we have to win the league at all costs, but we simply want consistent results. Our away performances have been poor. “The second reason is that, personally, I received reports that the technical team led by Karim Zito were not on good terms, and that could be affecting our results.” Zito joined AshantiGold in February 2026, 15 days after resigning from Kotoko, where he had been in charge. The former Dreams FC coach subsequently guided AshantiGold to promotion to the Ghana Premier League. Meanwhile, the club said that a caretaker coach would take charge of the team until a substantive head coach and technical director is appointed.

items.title: Petrol prices tipped to fall from Nov. 1 as diesel floor rises
items.description: Petrol prices could fall at the pump from November 1, 2026, while diesel prices may rise marginally after the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) adjusts its price floors. Market data obtained by JoyBusiness indicates that the petrol price floor has been reduced from GH¢16.09 to GH¢15.39 per litre for the November 1–15 pricing window. The diesel floor, however, has increased from GH¢17.09 to GH¢17.41 per litre. Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) could also see some relief, with its price floor declining from GH¢13.89 to GH¢13.73 per kilogram. These figures are price floors, not final retail prices. According to the NPA, they exclude premiums charged by International Oil Trading Companies, operating margins of Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies, and margins charged by Oil Marketing Companies and LPG Marketing Companies. The respective companies will determine those charges independently under the prescribed Petroleum Products Pricing Formula. Impact The adjustments could produce mixed price movements at the pumps during the next pricing window. Lower price floors could give marketers room to reduce petrol and LPG prices. However, final adjustments will depend on the premiums and margins individual companies apply. One major oil marketing company currently sells petrol at GH¢16.45 per litre and diesel at GH¢17.95 per litre. Some marketers could reduce prices, while others may leave them unchanged. The higher diesel floor also suggests upward pressure on its retail price. Although international crude oil prices have been rising, the cedi’s recent appreciation may help cushion some of the pressure on local fuel prices. Background and price quotes for October Petrol and diesel prices recorded marginal reductions at the pumps from October 16, 2026. LPG prices, however, were projected to rise by about 18.5% per kilogram. The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies attributed the petrol and diesel reductions to movements in international refined product prices and government subsidy measures. In its report for that period, the Chamber said average crude oil prices rose 2.03% to US$126.73 per barrel amid renewed supply concerns. Refined petroleum products recorded mixed movements. International LPG prices rose 7.77%, while diesel and petrol prices fell 6.68% and 3.93%, respectively. Over the same assessment period, the cedi depreciated by 1.61% to GH¢11.8222 per US dollar, based on average bank rates between September 26 and October 11, 2026. The Chamber said the currency had lost more than 11% against the dollar since the start of the year, with seasonal import demand and higher energy costs contributing to the pressure. Despite those pressures, lower international petrol and diesel prices, together with the subsidy measures, supported modest reductions at the pumps during the October 16 pricing window.

items.title: Guinée : Aïssata Sia Camara intègre le protocole d’État et s’offre un passeport diplomatique
items.description: Aïssata Sia Camara, infirmière de formation devenue ouvrière sur le chantier du futur siège de l’Assemblée nationale, bénéficie de plusieurs avantages après avoir attiré l’attention du président Mamadi Doumbouya à Koloma. Remarquée par le chef de l’État lors d’une visite du chantier, puis mise en avant lors d’une séance photo, elle vient d'être intégrée au protocole d’État à la Présidence de la République. Elle bénéfice également d’une maison et d’un passeport diplomatique. Selon les informations communiquées par la Direction de la Communication et de l'Information de la Présidence, Aïssata Sia Camara devrait prochainement suivre une formation en diplomatie pour se préparer à ses nouvelles fonctions.

items.title: Actes contre nature-transmission volontaire VIH : 4 individus arrêtés à Thiès
items.description: Quatre individus ont été arrêtés par la police pour des faits d'actes contre nature avec des personnes du même sexe et de transmission volontaire du virus de l'immunodéficience humaine (VIH). À l'issue de leur garde à vue, ils ont été déférés au parquet. Le poste de police de Nguinth a procédé, le 17 octobre 2026, à l'interpellation de quatre individus pour des faits d'actes contre nature avec des personnes du même sexe et de transmission volontaire du virus de l'immunodéficience humaine (VIH). « L'enquête a été ouverte à la suite de renseignements faisant état d'activités répréhensibles menées par le biais d'une application de rencontre. Les investigations menées par les services de police ont permis d'identifier et d'interpeller un premier suspect », explique la police à travers une note rendue publique mardi soir. Entendu sur les faits, ce dernier a reconnu, poursuit notre source, recevoir des partenaires masculins à son domicile pour des attouchements et des pratiques sexuelles, tout en précisant n'avoir eu qu'un seul rapport complet. A lire aussi : Bignona : un boutiquier interpellé pour des faits présumés de viols répétés sur des mineurs La poursuite des investigations a conduit à l'interpellation de trois autres individus impliqués. Une perquisition effectuée dans la chambre de l'un d'eux a permis de saisir divers effets. Il s’agit notamment de trois sachets de préservatifs non utilisés, de huit sachets de lubrifiant, de deux pots de baume cosmétique ainsi que d'une bouteille de lubrifiant intime. Interrogés à leur tour, les mis en cause ont admis avoir eu des relations sexuelles avec des partenaires masculins. « L'exploitation technique de leurs téléphones portables a permis de mettre en évidence des échanges à caractère érotique avec d'autres hommes, ainsi que des contenus multimédias à caractère pornographique et des documents visuels attestant de leurs pratiques », poursuit le texte. Par ailleurs, les analyses médicales et sérologiques réalisées ont révélé que trois de ces individus sont testés positifs au VIH. Mariama DIEME
